paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Tower Hamlets, including the council's own fostering service. Since May 2024 the council has recruited through Local Community Fostering, a joint service it runs with five other north-east London boroughs: Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, Newham and Redbridge. When it launched, the councils said London had about four children needing a foster home for every approved carer, and that the number of approved fostering households in the capital had fallen from 3,685 in 2014 to 2,560 by March 2023.

Tower Hamlets says foster carers come from all backgrounds and that anyone can foster whatever their religion, sexual orientation, ethnicity or circumstances, as long as they can give a child a loving and stable home. Its service is Family Friendly accredited, and carers get allowances, support around the clock, training and therapeutic support.

In May 2026 the council announced that its foster carers would pay no council tax from the 2026-27 financial year: a full reduction, refunded at the end of a carer's first year of approval, on top of the fostering allowances. The council also holds a yearly celebration for its foster and kinship carers; nearly 100 attended in October 2025, some of whom have fostered for more than 20 years.

If you are thinking about it, go to one of the council's information events, and speak to two or three of the services above about training, support and the children they most need homes for. If you live near the borough's edge, see the Newham, Hackney and London pages too.
